item.title: CVE-2026-59159 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.5
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.5 | Linux Mint Update Manager manages software updates on Linux Mint systems. From 5.4.8 until 5.5.4.3, 5.5.9.1, 5.8.8.1, 5.9.8.1, 6.0.9.1, and 6.1.5.1, mint-refresh-cache passes a user-controlled --parent-window-id value directly to the privileged Synaptic process without validating it as an integer. A local user permitted to execute mint-refresh-cache through sudo can inject additional Synaptic command-line options and achieve arbitrary code execution as root. This issue is fixed in versions 5.5.4.3, 5.5.9.1, 5.8.8.1, 5.9.8.1, 6.0.9.1, and 6.1.5.1.

item.title: CVE-2026-76411 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | A vulnerability in the phishcheck functionality of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device. This vulnerability is due to improper allocation of memory during processing of URLs. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a URL to be processed by the software. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

item.title: CVE-2026-76414 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | A vulnerability in Microsoft Compiled HTML Help (CHM) file scanning of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device. This vulnerability is due to a logic error when scanning the CHM file and following the internal file pointers. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted CHM file for scanning. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV decode process to terminate due to an infinite loop, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

item.title: CVE-2026-76415 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | A vulnerability in the Yoda'a Crytper (yC) Portable Executable (PE) unpacker of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device. . This vulnerability is due to lack of proper error checking for negative values when processing the PE file to be unpacked. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

item.title: CVE-2026-76416 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | A vulnerability in the InstallShield file parser of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device. This vulnerability is due to incomplete error checking when the InstallShield File Parser is performing a scan. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted InstallShield file to be scanned. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate due to an infinite loop, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

item.title: CVE-2026-76417 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | A vulnerability in Object Linking and Embedding, 2nd Generation (OLE2) file parser for ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device. This vulnerability is due to logic error when parsing specifically formatted files with the OLE2 file parser. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by by sending a crafted Microsoft Compound File Binary (CFB) file to be scanned. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to allocate all available memory, causing the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

item.title: CVE-2026-76421 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | A vulnerability in the LZX data algorithm for Microsoft Compiled HTML Help (CHM) file scanning in ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device. This vulnerability is due to improper boundary checks when applying the LZX data algorithm to CHM files during the decoder stage, which may result in buffer overflow. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted CHM file for scanning. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

item.title: CVE-2026-76430 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | A vulnerability in the Ultimate Packer for eXecutables (UPX) unpacker of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device. item.title: CVE-2026-76515 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | A vulnerability in the Object Linking and Embedding, 2nd Generation (OLE2) file parser for ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to exceed the configured MaxScanTime and cause a DoS condition on an affected device. This vulnerability is due to inefficiencies when parsing specifically formatted files with the OLE2 file parser. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by by sending a crafted Microsoft Compound File Binary (CFB) file to be scanned. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to effectively cause the ClamAV OLE2 parser to get into an infinite loop, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

item.title: CVE-2026-76516 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | A vulnerability in the eXtensible ARchive (XAR) GZIP file parser for ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to exceed the configured MaxFileSize and cause a DoS condition on an affected device. This vulnerability is due to inefficiencies when parsing specifically formatted files with the XAR GZIP file parser. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by by sending a crafted XAR GZIP file to be scanned. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to effectively cause the ClamAV to exceed the MaxFileSize and potentially get caught in an infinite loop, causing a DoS condition.
